water.en: A substance (of molecular formula H₂O) found at room temperature and pressure as a clear liquid; it is present naturally as rain, and found in rivers, lakes and seas; its solid form is ice and its gaseous form is steam.

food.en: Any solid substance that can be consumed by living organisms, especially by eating, in order to sustain life.

house.en: A structure built or serving as an abode of human beings.

school.en: (collective) A group of fish or a group of marine mammals such as porpoises, dolphins, or whales.

book.en: A collection of sheets of paper bound together to hinge at one edge, containing printed or written material, pictures, etc.

friend.en: A person other than a family member, spouse or lover whose company one enjoys and towards whom one feels affection.

family.en: A group of people who are closely related to one another (by blood, marriage or adoption); kin; for example, a set of parents and their children; an immediate family.

teacher.en: A person who teaches, especially one employed in a school.

student.en: A person who studies or learns about a particular subject.

morning.en: The part of the day from dawn to noon.

tomorrow.en: The day after the present day.

week.en: Any period of seven consecutive days.

month.en: A period into which a year is divided, historically based on the phases of the moon.

year.en: A solar year, the time it takes the Earth to complete one revolution of the Sun (between 365.24 and 365.26 days depending on the point of reference).

city.en: A large settlement, bigger than a town; sometimes with a specific legal definition, depending on the place.

country.en: (chiefly British) An area of land; a district, region.

money.en: A legally or socially binding conceptual contract of entitlement to wealth, void of intrinsic value, payable for all debts and taxes, and regulated in supply.

phone.en: A device for transmitting conversations and other sounds in real time across distances, now often a small portable unit also capable of running software etc.

table.en: Furniture with a top surface to accommodate a variety of uses.

chair.en: An item of furniture used to sit on or in, comprising a seat, legs, back, and sometimes arm rests, for use by one person. Compare stool, couch, sofa, settee, loveseat and bench.

door.en: A portal of entry into a building, room, or vehicle, consisting of a rigid plane movable on a hinge. Doors are frequently made of wood or metal. May have a handle to help open and close, a latch to hold the door closed and a lock that ensures the door cannot be opened without the key.

window.en: The inedible parts of a grain-producing plant.

car.en: A wheeled vehicle that moves independently, with at least three wheels, powered mechanically, steered by a driver and mostly for personal transportation.

bus.en: A motor vehicle for transporting large numbers of people along roads.

train.vi: xe lửa; rèn luyện, đào tạo

street.en: A paved part of road, usually in a village or a town.

shop.en: An establishment that sells goods or services to the public; originally only a physical location, but now a virtual establishment as well.

hospital.en: A large medical facility, usually in a building with multiple floors, where seriously ill or injured patients are given extensive medical and/or surgical treatment.

doctor.en: A physician; a member of the medical profession; one who is trained and licensed to heal the sick or injured. The final examination and qualification may award a doctor degree in which case the post-nominal letters are D.O., DPM, M.D., DMD, DDS, in the US or MBBS in the UK.
doctor.vi: bác sĩ y khoa, tiến sĩ

name.en: Any nounal word or phrase which indicates a particular person, place, class, or thing.

time.en: The inevitable progression into the future with the passing of present and past events.

kitchen.en: A room or area for preparing food.

garden.en: An outdoor area containing one or more types of plants, usually plants grown for food or ornamental purposes.

flower.en: A colorful, conspicuous structure associated with angiosperms, frequently scented and attracting various insects, and which may or may not be used for sexual reproduction.

animal.en: In scientific usage, a multicellular organism that is usually mobile, whose cells are not encased in a rigid cell wall (distinguishing it from plants and fungi) and which derives energy solely from the consumption of other organisms (distinguishing it from plants).

dog.en: A mammal, Canis familiaris or Canis lupus familiaris, that has been domesticated for thousands of years, of highly variable appearance due to human breeding.

cat.en: An animal of the family Felidae:

bird.en: A member of the class of animals Aves in the phylum Chordata, characterized by being warm-blooded, having feathers and wings usually capable of flight, and laying eggs.

fish.en: A cold-blooded vertebrate animal that lives in water, moving with the help of fins and breathing with gills.

milk.en: A white liquid produced by the mammary glands of female mammals to nourish their young. From certain animals, especially cows, it is also called dairy milk and is a common food for humans as a beverage or used to produce various dairy products such as butter, cheese, and yogurt.

bread.en: A foodstuff made by baking dough made from cereals.

rice.en: Cereal plants, Oryza sativa of the grass family whose seeds are used as food.

meat.en: The flesh (muscle tissue) of an animal used as food.

egg.en: An approximately spherical or ellipsoidal body produced by birds, reptiles, insects and other animals, housing the embryo during its development.

apple.en: A common, round fruit produced by the tree Malus domestica, cultivated in temperate climates.

orange.en: An evergreen tree of the genus Citrus such as Citrus sinensis.

banana.en: An elongated curved tropical fruit that grows in bunches and has a creamy flesh and a smooth skin.

coffee.en: A beverage made by infusing the beans of the coffee plant in hot water.

sugar.en: Sucrose in the form of small crystals, obtained from sugar cane or sugar beet and used to sweeten food and drink.

salt.en: A common substance, chemically consisting mainly of sodium chloride (NaCl), used extensively as a condiment and preservative.

hot.en: (with up) To heat; to make or become hot.

cold.en: (of a thing) Having a low temperature.

big.en: Someone or something that is large in stature

small.en: Any part of something that is smaller or slimmer than the rest, now usually with anatomical reference to the back.

good.vi: tốt, hay, tuyệt; điểu tốt, điều thiện

happy.en: A happy event, thing, person, etc.

sad.en: To make melancholy; to sadden or grieve (someone).

old.en: (with the, invariable plural only) People who are old; old beings; the older generation, taken as a group.

young.en: People who are young; young people, collectively; youth.

tall.en: (possibly nonstandard) Someone or something that is tall.

fast.en: A train that calls at only some stations it passes between its origin and destination, typically just the principal stations

slow.en: Someone who is slow; a sluggard.

hard.en: A firm or paved beach or slope convenient for hauling vessels out of the water.
hard.vi: cứng, rắn, hà khắc; hết sức cố gắng, tích cực

open.vi: mở, ngỏ; bắt đầu, khai mạc
